requirement: Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST NOT offer a waiver for an uncited first-party Rust function. When a function serves only as an internal implementation detail and no existing requirement explains it, Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST direct agents to propose an explicit project requirement, such as `internal-detail`, obtain the user's agreement, cite it on the function, and record evidence explaining why each such function introduces no additional end-user-observable behavior. An internal-detail requirement MUST NOT justify an otherwise unspecified end-user-observable behavior.
rationale: All three bundled skills prohibit uncited-function waivers. They direct agents to propose an agreed internal-detail requirement when needed, cite it on each function, and record evidence that the function adds no otherwise unspecified observable behavior.

text: Add a requirement or example reference in a Rust comment attached to each inventoried function or method or within its body. An example must cite a requirement, so an example reference still traces the function to a requirement. A reference on an enclosing module or `impl` does not cover its functions. There is no waiver for an uncited function. If no behavior-specific requirement explains an internal helper, propose an explicit project requirement such as `internal-detail`, get the user's agreement, and cite it. Record evidence explaining why each such function adds no end-user-observable behavior beyond the requirements it supports. Do not use an internal-detail requirement to justify unspecified end-user-visible behavior.

When checking a determination against code, inspect every end-user-observable result and branch, including errors and input handling. Confirm that the code does what each applicable requirement says and introduces no additional observable behavior without an agreed requirement. When requirements interact, cite every applicable requirement at the relevant implementation point and explain in the rationale how their texts jointly account for the behavior. A citation alone does not prove the behavior is specified.

Every explicit function or method in first-party Rust sources needs its own requirement or example reference, including trait methods and test helpers. Each example cites a requirement. Do not waive an uncited function because it is an internal helper. If no behavior-specific requirement explains it, propose an explicit project requirement such as `internal-detail` for the user's agreement, cite it, and give evidence for each such function explaining why it introduces no additional end-user-observable behavior. Do not use internal-detail to justify unspecified observable behavior.
